passages.text: Some time later, when the anger of King Xerxes had subsided, he remembered Vashti and what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled a vast kingdom.
He became angry with Queen Vashti.
After some time, his anger faded.
King Xerxes remembered Vashti.
He remembered what Vashti had done.
He also remembered what had been decreed against Vashti.
passages.original: אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה כְּשֹׁ֕ךְ חֲמַ֖ת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֑וֹשׁ זָכַ֤ר אֶת־ וַשְׁתִּי֙ וְאֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֔תָה וְאֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ נִגְזַ֖ר עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Then the king’s attendants proposed, “Let a search be made for beautiful young virgins for the king, and let the king appoint commissioners in each province of his kingdom to assemble all the beautiful young women into the harem at the citadel of Susa. Let them be placed under the care of Hegai, the king’s eunuch in charge of the women, and let them be given beauty treatments.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled a vast kingdom.
He had many attendants who served him.
The attendants spoke to the king.
They said, “Let us search for young women who are virgins and beautiful.”
They wanted to find these women for the king.
They suggested that the king appoint officials in every province of his kingdom.
These officials would gather every beautiful young virgin.
They would bring them to the citadel of Susa.
They would place the women in the house for women.
Hegai was the king’s eunuch.
Hegai was in charge of the women.
The women would be under Hegai’s care.
They would receive beauty treatments.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ נַעֲרֵֽי־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מְשָׁרְתָ֑יו יְבַקְשׁ֥וּ לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ נְעָר֥וֹת בְּתוּל֖וֹת טוֹב֥וֹת מַרְאֶֽה׃ וְיַפְקֵ֨ד הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ פְּקִידִים֮ בְּכָל־ מְדִינ֣וֹת מַלְכוּתוֹ֒ וְיִקְבְּצ֣וּ אֶת־ כָּל־ נַעֲרָֽה־ בְ֠תוּלָה טוֹבַ֨ת מַרְאֶ֜ה אֶל־ שׁוּשַׁ֤ן הַבִּירָה֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית הַנָּשִׁ֔ים אֶל־ יַ֥ד הֵגֶ֛א סְרִ֥יס הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמֵ֣ר הַנָּשִׁ֑ים וְנָת֖וֹן תַּמְרוּקֵיהֶֽן׃

passages.text: Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen in place of Vashti.” This suggestion pleased the king, and he acted accordingly.
passages.sermon:
The king of Persia was named Xerxes.
He had removed Queen Vashti from her position.
The king’s attendants suggested a plan to find a new queen.
They said, “Let the young woman who pleases the king become queen instead of Vashti.”
The king liked this suggestion.
The king decided to follow this plan.
passages.original: וְהַֽנַּעֲרָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר תִּיטַב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ תִּמְלֹ֖ךְ תַּ֣חַת וַשְׁתִּ֑י וַיִּיטַ֧ב הַדָּבָ֛ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיַּ֥עַשׂ כֵּֽן׃ס

passages.text: Now there was at the citadel of Susa a Jewish man from the tribe of Benjamin named Mordecai son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish.
passages.sermon:
A Jewish man lived in the citadel of Susa.
His name was Mordecai.
Mordecai was the son of Jair.
Jair was the son of Shimei.
Shimei was the son of Kish.
Mordecai belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
passages.original: אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדִ֔י הָיָ֖ה בְּשׁוּשַׁ֣ן הַבִּירָ֑ה וּשְׁמ֣וֹ מָרְדֳּכַ֗י בֶּ֣ן יָאִ֧יר בֶּן־ שִׁמְעִ֛י בֶּן־ קִ֖ישׁ אִ֥ישׁ יְמִינִֽי׃

passages.text: He had been carried into exile from Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon among those taken captive with Jeconiah king of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He took people from Jerusalem into exile.
Jeconiah was the king of Judah at that time.
Mordecai was among those taken captive with Jeconiah.
Nebuchadnezzar carried Mordecai and others away from Jerusalem.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָגְלָה֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלַ֔יִם עִם־ הַגֹּלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָגְלְתָ֔ה עִ֖ם יְכָנְיָ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶגְלָ֔ה נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֖ר מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: And Mordecai had brought up Hadassah (that is, Esther), the daughter of his uncle, because she did not have a father or mother. The young woman was lovely in form and appearance, and when her father and mother had died, Mordecai had taken her in as his own daughter.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jewish man from the tribe of Benjamin.
He lived in the citadel of Susa.
Mordecai had a relative named Hadassah.
Her other name was Esther.
Esther was the daughter of Mordecai’s uncle.
Esther did not have a father or mother.
Esther was a young woman.
She was beautiful in form.
She was beautiful in appearance.
Esther’s father and mother died.
Mordecai took Esther as his own daughter.
He raised her in his home.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֨י אֹמֵ֜ן אֶת־ הֲדַסָּ֗ה הִ֤יא אֶסְתֵּר֙ בַּת־ דֹּד֔וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין לָ֖הּ אָ֣ב וָאֵ֑ם וְהַנַּעֲרָ֤ה יְפַת־ תֹּ֙אַר֙ וְטוֹבַ֣ת מַרְאֶ֔ה וּבְמ֤וֹת אָבִ֙יהָ֙ וְאִמָּ֔הּ לְקָחָ֧הּ מָרְדֳּכַ֛י ל֖וֹ לְבַֽת׃

passages.text: When the king’s command and edict had been proclaimed, many young women gathered at the citadel of Susa under the care of Hegai. Esther was also taken to the palace and placed under the care of Hegai, the custodian of the women.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes gave a command and an edict.
People heard the king’s command and edict.
Many young women gathered at the citadel of Susa.
Hegai cared for these young women.
Esther was among the young women.
People took Esther to the king’s palace.
Hegai, the custodian of the women, cared for Esther in the palace.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בְּהִשָּׁמַ֤ע דְּבַר־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וְדָת֔וֹ וּֽבְהִקָּבֵ֞ץ נְעָר֥וֹת רַבּ֛וֹת אֶל־ שׁוּשַׁ֥ן הַבִּירָ֖ה אֶל־ יַ֣ד הֵגָ֑י וַתִּלָּקַ֤ח אֶסְתֵּר֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֶל־ יַ֥ד הֵגַ֖י שֹׁמֵ֥ר הַנָּשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: And the young woman pleased him and obtained his favor, so he quickly provided her with beauty treatments and the special diet. He assigned to her seven select maidservants from the palace and transferred her with them to the best place in the harem.
passages.sermon:
Esther was a young woman.
Esther was lovely in form and appearance.
Hegai was the custodian of the women in the king’s palace.
Esther pleased Hegai.
Esther found favor in Hegai’s eyes.
Hegai quickly gave Esther her beauty treatments.
Hegai quickly gave Esther her special food.
Hegai assigned seven select maidservants from the king’s palace to Esther.
Hegai moved Esther and her maidservants to the best place in the harem.
passages.original: וַתִּיטַ֨ב הַנַּעֲרָ֣ה בְעֵינָיו֮ וַתִּשָּׂ֣א חֶ֣סֶד לְפָנָיו֒ וַ֠יְבַהֵל אֶת־ תַּמְרוּקֶ֤יהָ וְאֶת־ מָנוֹתֶ֙הָ֙ לָתֵ֣ת לָ֔הּ וְאֵת֙ שֶׁ֣בַע הַנְּעָר֔וֹת הָרְאֻי֥וֹת לָֽתֶת־ לָ֖הּ מִבֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיְשַׁנֶּ֧הָ וְאֶת־ נַעֲרוֹתֶ֛יהָ לְט֖וֹב בֵּ֥ית הַנָּשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: Esther did not reveal her people or her lineage, because Mordecai had instructed her not to do so.
passages.sermon:
Esther was a young Jewish woman.
She lived in the citadel of Susa.
Esther did not tell anyone about her people.
She did not reveal her family background.
Mordecai was her cousin and guardian.
Mordecai told Esther not to reveal her people or her lineage.
Esther obeyed Mordecai’s instruction.
passages.original: לֹא־ הִגִּ֣ידָה אֶסְתֵּ֔ר אֶת־ עַמָּ֖הּ וְאֶת־ מֽוֹלַדְתָּ֑הּ כִּ֧י מָרְדֳּכַ֛י צִוָּ֥ה עָלֶ֖יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ תַגִּֽיד׃

passages.text: And every day Mordecai would walk back and forth in front of the court of the harem to learn about Esther’s welfare and what was happening to her.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was Esther’s cousin and guardian.
Every day, Mordecai walked in front of the courtyard of the harem.
He wanted to know how Esther was doing.
He wanted to learn what was happening to her.
passages.original: וּבְכָל־ י֣וֹם וָי֔וֹם מָרְדֳּכַי֙ מִתְהַלֵּ֔ךְ לִפְנֵ֖י חֲצַ֣ר בֵּית־ הַנָּשִׁ֑ים לָדַ֙עַת֙ אֶת־ שְׁל֣וֹם אֶסְתֵּ֔ר וּמַה־ יֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: In the twelve months before her turn to go to King Xerxes, the harem regulation required each young woman to receive beauty treatments with oil of myrrh for six months, and then with perfumes and cosmetics for another six months.
passages.sermon:
Each young woman waited for her turn to go to King Xerxes.
The harem had a regulation for all the women.
Each woman completed twelve months of preparation before meeting the king.
For the first six months, she received beauty treatments with oil of myrrh.
For the next six months, she received perfumes and cosmetics.
These treatments prepared each woman for her time with the king.
passages.original: וּבְהַגִּ֡יעַ תֹּר֩ נַעֲרָ֨ה וְנַעֲרָ֜ה לָב֣וֹא׀ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֗וֹשׁ מִקֵּץ֩ הֱי֨וֹת לָ֜הּ כְּדָ֤ת הַנָּשִׁים֙ שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֣ר חֹ֔דֶשׁ כִּ֛י כֵּ֥ן יִמְלְא֖וּ יְמֵ֣י מְרוּקֵיהֶ֑ן שִׁשָּׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ בְּשֶׁ֣מֶן הַמֹּ֔ר וְשִׁשָּׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ בַּבְּשָׂמִ֔ים וּבְתַמְרוּקֵ֖י הַנָּשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: When the young woman would go to the king, she was given whatever she requested to take with her from the harem to the king’s palace.
passages.sermon:
A young woman would go to the king.
She came from the harem.
She could ask for anything to take with her.
She received whatever she requested.
She brought these things with her to the king’s palace.
passages.original: וּבָזֶ֕ה הַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה בָּאָ֣ה אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ אֵת֩ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תֹּאמַ֜ר יִנָּ֤תֵֽן לָהּ֙ לָב֣וֹא עִמָּ֔הּ מִבֵּ֥ית הַנָּשִׁ֖ים עַד־ בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: She would go there in the evening, and in the morning she would return to a second harem under the care of Shaashgaz, the king’s eunuch in charge of the concubines. She would not return to the king unless he delighted in her and summoned her by name.
passages.sermon:
The young woman would go to the king in the evening.
In the morning, she would return to a second harem.
Shaashgaz was the king’s eunuch.
Shaashgaz was in charge of the concubines.
The young woman would stay in the second harem under Shaashgaz’s care.
She would not return to the king again.
She could only return if the king delighted in her.
The king had to call her by name for her to return.
passages.original: בָּעֶ֣רֶב׀ הִ֣יא בָאָ֗ה וּ֠בַבֹּקֶר הִ֣יא שָׁבָ֞ה אֶל־ בֵּ֤ית הַנָּשִׁים֙ שֵׁנִ֔י אֶל־ יַ֧ד שַֽׁעֲשְׁגַ֛ז סְרִ֥יס הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמֵ֣ר הַפִּֽילַגְשִׁ֑ים לֹא־ תָב֥וֹא עוֹד֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֣י אִם־ חָפֵ֥ץ בָּ֛הּ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְנִקְרְאָ֥ה בְשֵֽׁם׃

passages.text: Now Esther was the daughter of Abihail, the uncle from whom Mordecai had adopted her as his own daughter. And when it was her turn to go to the king, she did not ask for anything except what Hegai, the king’s trusted official in charge of the harem, had advised. And Esther found favor in the eyes of everyone who saw her.
passages.sermon:
Esther was the daughter of Abihail.
Abihail was the uncle of Mordecai.
Mordecai had adopted Esther as his own daughter.
It became Esther’s turn to go to the king.
Esther did not ask for anything to take with her.
She only accepted what Hegai advised her to take.
Hegai was the king’s trusted official.
Hegai was in charge of the harem.
Everyone who saw Esther liked her.
Esther found favor in the eyes of all who saw her.
passages.original: וּבְהַגִּ֣יעַ תֹּר־ אֶסְתֵּ֣ר בַּת־ אֲבִיחַ֣יִל דֹּ֣ד מָרְדֳּכַ֡י אֲשֶׁר֩ לָקַֽח־ ל֨וֹ לְבַ֜ת לָב֣וֹא אֶל־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ לֹ֤א בִקְשָׁה֙ דָּבָ֔ר כִּ֠י אִ֣ם אֶת־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֹאמַ֛ר הֵגַ֥י סְרִיס־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמֵ֣ר הַנָּשִׁ֑ים וַתְּהִ֤י אֶסְתֵּר֙ נֹשֵׂ֣את חֵ֔ן בְּעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־ רֹאֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: She was taken to King Xerxes in the royal palace in the tenth month, the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
passages.sermon:
Esther was a young Jewish woman.
King Xerxes ruled over a vast empire.
Esther was taken to King Xerxes.
She entered the royal palace.
This happened in the tenth month.
The tenth month is called Tebeth.
It was the seventh year of King Xerxes’ reign.
passages.original: וַתִּלָּקַ֨ח אֶסְתֵּ֜ר אֶל־ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית מַלְכוּת֔וֹ בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֖י הוּא־ חֹ֣דֶשׁ טֵבֵ֑ת בִּשְׁנַת־ שֶׁ֖בַע לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And the king loved Esther more than all the other women, and she found grace and favor in his sight more than all of the other virgins. So he placed the royal crown upon her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled over Persia.
He chose a new queen after Vashti.
King Xerxes loved Esther more than all the other women.
Esther pleased the king more than all the other virgins.
Esther found grace and favor in the king’s eyes.
The king placed the royal crown on Esther’s head.
The king made Esther queen instead of Vashti.
passages.original: וַיֶּאֱהַ֨ב הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֶת־ אֶסְתֵּר֙ מִכָּל־ הַנָּשִׁ֔ים וַתִּשָּׂא־ חֵ֥ן וָחֶ֛סֶד לְפָנָ֖יו מִכָּל־ הַבְּתוּלֹ֑ת וַיָּ֤שֶׂם כֶּֽתֶר־ מַלְכוּת֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֔הּ וַיַּמְלִיכֶ֖הָ תַּ֥חַת וַשְׁתִּֽי׃

passages.text: Then the king held a great banquet, Esther’s banquet, for all his officials and servants. He proclaimed a tax holiday in the provinces and gave gifts worthy of the king’s bounty.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes was the ruler.
He held a great banquet.
This banquet was called Esther’s banquet.
He invited all his officials.
He invited all his servants.
He proclaimed a tax holiday in the provinces.
He gave gifts.
These gifts were generous, as only a king could give.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ מִשְׁתֶּ֣ה גָד֗וֹל לְכָל־ שָׂרָיו֙ וַעֲבָדָ֔יו אֵ֖ת מִשְׁתֵּ֣ה אֶסְתֵּ֑ר וַהֲנָחָ֤ה לַמְּדִינוֹת֙ עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֥ן מַשְׂאֵ֖ת כְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: When the virgins were assembled a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew.
Mordecai cared for Esther.
The king of Persia ruled a great empire.
The king gathered young women for his court.
The king assembled the virgins a second time.
Mordecai sat at the king’s gate during this time.
passages.original: וּבְהִקָּבֵ֥ץ בְּתוּל֖וֹת שֵׁנִ֑ית וּמָרְדֳּכַ֖י יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּשַֽׁעַר־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Esther still had not revealed her lineage or her people, just as Mordecai had instructed. She obeyed Mordecai’s command, as she had done under his care.
passages.sermon:
Esther was a Jewish woman living in the Persian court.
Esther did not reveal her family background.
Esther did not reveal her people.
Mordecai had instructed Esther to keep this secret.
Esther obeyed Mordecai’s command.
Esther continued to obey Mordecai just as she had when he raised her.
passages.original: אֵ֣ין אֶסְתֵּ֗ר מַגֶּ֤דֶת מֽוֹלַדְתָּהּ֙ וְאֶת־ עַמָּ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה עָלֶ֖יהָ מָרְדֳּכָ֑י וְאֶת־ מַאֲמַ֤ר מָרְדֳּכַי֙ אֶסְתֵּ֣ר עֹשָׂ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר הָיְתָ֥ה בְאָמְנָ֖ה אִתּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs who guarded the entrance, grew angry and conspired to assassinate King Xerxes.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew.
He was sitting at the king’s gate.
This happened during the days of King Xerxes.
Bigthan and Teresh were two of the king’s eunuchs.
They guarded the entrance to the palace.
Bigthan and Teresh became angry.
They planned to harm King Xerxes.
They conspired to assassinate the king.
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם וּמָרְדֳּכַ֖י יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּשַֽׁעַר־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ קָצַף֩ בִּגְתָ֨ן וָתֶ֜רֶשׁ שְׁנֵֽי־ סָרִיסֵ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ מִשֹּׁמְרֵ֣י הַסַּ֔ף וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ לִשְׁלֹ֣חַ יָ֔ד בַּמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵֽרֹשׁ׃

passages.text: When Mordecai learned of the plot, he reported it to Queen Esther, and she informed the king on Mordecai’s behalf.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew living in Persia.
Mordecai learned about a plot against King Xerxes.
Mordecai told Queen Esther about the plot.
Esther was the queen of Persia.
Esther told the king about the plot.
Esther told the king that Mordecai had discovered the plot.
passages.original: וַיִּוָּדַ֤ע הַדָּבָר֙ לְמָרְדֳּכַ֔י וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֑ה וַתֹּ֧אמֶר אֶסְתֵּ֛ר לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּשֵׁ֥ם מָרְדֳּכָֽי׃

passages.text: After the report had been investigated and verified, both officials were hanged on the gallows. And all this was recorded in the Book of the Chronicles in the presence of the king.
passages.sermon:
Officials investigated the report about the plot.
They found the report to be true.
They hanged both officials on a tree.
They wrote all these events in the Book of the Chronicles.
The king saw this record.
passages.original: וַיְבֻקַּ֤שׁ הַדָּבָר֙ וַיִּמָּצֵ֔א וַיִּתָּל֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־ עֵ֑ץ וַיִּכָּתֵ֗ב בְּסֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ
